ui.note: baselineBytes: the ui page-load graph (dist/ui/index.js and its static imports, esbuild-minified, gzip -9) at 6ade3a0, before the in-chat media work. marginBytes: what the core media work may add: story 0 (media kinds, IRI and @id reading, page_open reports) +1.9 KB, story 1 (pictures, figure cards, safe URLs) +1.6 KB, story 2 (detection, the access gate, play buttons in both views, the first tap, the latest-episode fetch) +3.2 KB. The player itself is the lazy media chunk, not counted here. Then +3.0 KB for a remote agent's answer drawn as cards (the handoff `answer` part read and tidied, the cited cards, compact rows, and the link check for replies). Then +0.25 KB for 👍 and 👎 on a remote answer: the controller's feedback send, the answer's task, and the loader. The controls themselves (their DOM, styles and state) are a lazy chunk, loaded with the first answer that has an answerId. Then +0.5 KB for the header's window / full-screen toggle (its button, two icons, labels, styles, the stored choice and the nxis-mode-change event). Then +213 B for the guardrails: the loader and its fail-closed check, the hooks every turn passes through (input, the provider wrapper, the tool stage, the bound approval, the guarded run, a card's navigation), untrusted text kept apart as `data`, and the element's `guardrails` property with `lockdown`. With the 87 B that was left, that is the story's 300 B. The rules themselves are the lazy guardrails chunk, not counted here. Then +53 B so a second copy of the harness on a page (two versions, or the CDN build beside a bundled one) loads without throwing: @a2ui/lit defines its elements unguarded as it evaluates, so src/a2ui/define-once.ts skips a name already defined around that import, and define-restore.ts puts the registry's own define back. Then +431 B for `contained`: the window and its launcher drawn in the host's box as a preview, its property, the CSS that positions them against the box, what it turns off (discovery, preloading and loading the on-device model, stored conversations, resumed actions, and taking focus on connect), and its input off by default (the disabled composer, its placeholder, inert chips, and `allow-input` to turn it back on). Then +86 B for opening and closing from the page: `close()`, `isOpen`, and the `nxis-agent-toggle` event on every change. Then +1,942 B for event cards: the renderer spec's `happening` block, the answer view's hooks for events (the views and the tap, a lone event, rows, and the pick), loading the event cards' chunk and handing it the element's links, reports and form start, the calendar address from discovery, the handoff link's report token, and keeping the conversation when a handoff arrives from this chat. The cards themselves are the lazy `events` chunk, not counted here. Then +1,687 B for search forms as reads and the records first: a `method="get"` form's read-only test, its results URL and the visit that keeps the conversation, page titles in place of paths, form nouns in place of form ids, `when`, `from` and `to` on nxis_query with today's date, and the descriptions and instructions that put the site's records before a page's form. Reading a time and filtering records by it is a lazy chunk (`when`), not counted here. Then +2,240 B for one tool per form: grouping a site's forms by their endpoint, `nxis:fixedInput` read and used as the chooser, choices named by page title or the code in words, the merged schema's widened limits, checking a call against the chosen form's own fields with its tiers and limits in the refusal, sending only those fields, the card's "Get passes for", and the registry suffix dropped from every name a visitor reads. Then +38 B so a dated search that finds nothing never ends on "No results found.": the answer view reads the result's `notice` and says it, before the next events or in their place. Searching again from now on and wording the time is in the lazy `when` chunk, not counted here. Then +890 B so a turn never ends on result cards alone: after a read the model is asked again, to read on or answer in words (the answer step, its three bounds, the one nudge and its fallback lines, a read confirmed or completed later carried on to its answer and dropped when a newer turn starts, and the type listing's wording). Then +560 B for a handoff target's step surfaces (the Quote and Booking steps): the controller reading a reply's `surface` parts and sending an `action` part with the visitor's words, the thread item that keeps them, loading their chunk with the first reply that has one, the renderer kit handed to it (so Lit, the renderer and zod stay in this graph's chunk), and a choice sent through the same input checks as typed words. The components, the strict reading and the routing are the lazy `surfaces` chunk, not counted here. Then +64 B so Chrome's native tools reach a model proxy with their names: the handoff tools built rather than spread, and a tool with no name left out of the request with a warning instead of sending one the model API refuses. Then +128 B so a tool runs on Chrome 158, whose executeTool takes only the Tool object getTools() returned: when the registry refuses the tool given (a copy, such as a handoff tool built for the turn, a stand-in, or none), the registry's own object for that name is read and called before falling back to the name. Then +1,935 B for a test run's fixes: +124 B so the site actions this page can't run are said once a tab session at debug level, not as a warning on every load; +974 B so a visitor never reads a schema.org name (the technical types, a card's type in words, a search's plumbing left out, and loading a type listing's labels in place; the labels themselves are the lazy `type-tiles` chunk, about 1.2 KB); and +837 B for replies drawn as markdown and the page assistant's citations (the loader and the fill of a reply's bubble, the markdown renderer A2UI Text asks its Lit context for, the guardrails' check on a link drawn in a reply, and keeping a turn's records with its answer; the renderer itself is the lazy `markdown` chunk, about 1.7 KB, and matching an answer to its records is in the lazy `sources` chunk). Then +648 B so the visitor gives their details once per conversation: the profile's conversation layer (kept with the conversation, read with the host's preferences, cleared with "Not you? Clear details"), what a visitor sends on a form or a target's step kept, a hand-back's `contact` read strictly, and the profile sent as an agent target's envelope `contact`. Then +1,253 B for a second test run's fixes (23,096 B with them, after the visitor's details): nothing in the thread shrinks (an answer with Sources had become a 20 px sliver); an emergency turn's cards call the emergency line first (the emergency words, finding the line on a record, its seller or a contact point, and the reorder); a record also cited by the places it serves and its seller's phone; a card waiting for its button goes inert when the visitor types instead, and the model is told nothing was sent; the handoff bar at the top in the accent's wash, with its Heroicon and the agent named; an accent alone bringing its pressed shade and wash; the panel's title cut short with its name on hover; and an estimate's Sources waiting for its card to go under it. Less the type listing's tiles, which are no longer drawn (the lazy `type-tiles` chunk is gone). Then +344 B for a third test run's fixes (23,508 B with them): a hand-back's `next` read strictly and its Hand over card drawn at once without asking the model (one turn path for a typed message and a call already decided, the offer waiting for the hand-back to settle), the agent handoff tool told a question about what was already done is answered from the hand-back, and the panel reopening at the end of the thread or where the visitor left it. Superseded step cards, the held window and keeping a card's unsent edits are in the lazy `surfaces` chunk, not counted here. Then +354 B for a fourth test run's fixes (23,874 B with them): a declined handoff or form written into the conversation as not sent, the agent handoff tool told a question about the business is answered from the records, an answer that reads no records cited from those this conversation read earlier, and the panel opening again after a reload when it was open. The ReceiptCard's phone link is in the lazy `surfaces` chunk, not counted here. Then +446 B for a fifth test run's fixes (24,320 B with them): a read's records said with their hours in 12-hour time, each by name (the hours read into words, Monday first, days with the same hours together, round-the-clock hours as 24 hours), the handoff tools told never to take a request unrelated to the site, and an answer from earlier reads never cited for naming a record alone. The disabled and superseded buttons' looks are in the lazy `surfaces` chunk (12,239 B, under its budget), and listing records of one name once is in the lazy `sources` chunk, neither counted here. Then +518 B for a sixth test run's fixes (24,838 B with them): a results card that lists one business once (records of one name, type and address as one row, a pick moved to the row it is in), every call link in E.164, the thread kept at its end when step cards draw after a reload, each record's hours kept as the words that cite it, and the hours said for the model with what each record is (the business, its emergency service). Keeping a card's edits at once, a press sending what is on screen and an ended card's buttons disabled are in the lazy `surfaces` chunk; citing hours to their record is in the lazy `sources` chunk. Then +861 B for a seventh test run's fixes (25,699 B with them, so the margin goes from 24,896 to 25,792 B): the business's opening hours as its owner keeps them, from the proxy's policy copy (`openingHours`, read strictly), setting the results card's open status for the business's own records in the business's time zone (its wall clock read with Intl, closed dates, the next opening), its emergency service keeping its own hours, and a hand-back's `next` for a person target drawing the team's hand-over card as it does an agent's. Then +256 B (25,873 B with it, so the margin goes from 25,792 to 26,048 B) for a handoff the target ends at once: after a stream that brought nothing or broke, or a message refused because the task has ended, the controller reads the task once with GetTask and shows how it ended, sharing that read with readOnce.

media.note: The ./media chunk (src/media/*, loaded by a dynamic import() on the first Play tap) with whatever it alone pulls in, gzip -9.

guardrails.note: The ./guardrails chunk (src/guardrails/*, loaded by a dynamic import() at the first open or send, and awaited by every turn) with whatever it alone pulls in, gzip -9. Raised from 8192 to 8213 (+21 B) for a system prompt the model proxy holds (remote guardrails, part 4): the policy hook on the configuration and dropping the page's prompt for a remote model. Raised from 8213 to 8447 (+234 B) for the model proxy's policy (remote guardrails, part 5): loading the policy chunk when the element has guardrails-src, the version sent and checked on each completion, and a proxy's typed refusal said with the page's own message and reported as an nxis-guardrail event. Raised from 8447 to 8560 (+113 B) for kill switch messages that say which scope is off: the whole agent, or only its actions. Raised from 8560 to 8640 (+80 B) for copying each tool field by field when its description is wrapped, since Chrome's native tools keep their fields on the prototype and a spread dropped them, name and schema included.

guardrailsRemote.note: The chunk that fetches the model proxy's guardrails policy (src/guardrails/remote.ts and policy-core.ts, loaded by a dynamic import() from the guardrails only when the element has guardrails-src), gzip -9. It shares the guardrails' settingsFor and glob rather than splitting them into a chunk of their own, which would cost the guardrails chunk about 600 B in lost compression.

events.note: The event cards' chunk (src/ui/event-cards.ts, with the event model src/harness/happening.ts and the A2UI surfaces src/a2ui/events.ts, loaded by a dynamic import() with the first result that is an event) with whatever it alone pulls in, gzip -9. About 8.3 KB at its introduction.

surfaces.note: A handoff target's step surfaces' chunk (src/ui/surfaces.ts, with the steps catalog's components src/a2ui/steps-catalog.ts and the strict reading of a surface part src/a2ui/steps.ts, loaded by a dynamic import() with the first reply that has a surface) with whatever it alone pulls in, gzip -9. About 8.3 KB at its introduction. Raised from 9216 to 10752 for the guided intake (ui.surfaces 2), 10,304 B with it (+1,841 B): ChoiceChips (chips, the segmented control, several choices, More), StepHeader (the step line and its progress bar), FieldNote (a line with a Heroicon for its tone), their styles and three more Heroicons, their strict reading (choice, step and tone limits), and the step surface's label tokens and full width. Raised from 10752 to 11264 for field markers and errors (ui.surfaces 3), 10,873 B with it: the steps catalog's own TextField (the basic one's props with required, optional and error), "Required" and "Optional" after a label, an error drawn as a warn FieldNote under its field, and their strict reading. Raised from 11264 to 11776 for a second test run's fixes (the CDN chunk 10,776 -> 11,222 B gzip -9, +446 B): a TextField's inputType and autocomplete and their strict reading, a field's error cleared as it is edited, inset Estimate, Confirm and Receipt cards, a primary button that fills its row (a weighted basic Button too), and plain review labels and heading. Raised from 11776 to 12288 for a third test run's fixes (11,497 -> 11,921 B gzip -9, +424 B): superseded surfaces (a reply count on each surface, the newest made, inert and dimmed in gray, nothing sent from one), countdowns that stop and never send their action on a superseded surface, a WindowGrid window's `held`, and a live surface's unsent edits kept with the conversation and drawn again after a reload. Raised from 12288 to 12800 for a sixth test run's fixes (12,239 -> 12,588 B gzip -9, +349 B): a card's edits kept as they are made (on input and change, and when the page is hidden), a press reading the fields on screen into the card before it sends, a TextField taking its value on change too, and an ended or superseded card's buttons and fields disabled, not only out of reach.

lazyChunk.note: Every lazy chunk of the ui entry without a budget of its own (today the sources panel, about 3.7 KB with the page assistant's citations, the feedback controls, about 2.5 KB, and the markdown renderer, about 1.7 KB, each loaded by a dynamic import() on first use), with whatever it alone pulls in, gzip -9.

cdnProxy.note: The CDN build's proxy.js (createProxyProvider, self-contained), which a page imports beside ui.js to point the element at a model proxy, gzip -9. Built apart from ui.js so ui.js stays exactly the ./ui bundle measured above.
